assumptions: The DJ place (the owner's green, 2026-09-28) is a riser of stage decks 3 m wide x 2 m deep x 1.2 m high ON THE NAVE CENTRE LINE (x 0; the owner, 04:13: 'make the scene in center'), its back edge 1.0 m in front of the press's face (z 3.2 m, +-1.5 m), facing the entry and the crowd. The press stays where it stands, 1.65 m right of the axis (range 0.5-3.5), behind the right half of the riser. Three 2 x 1 m decks on 1.2 m legs; 'a bit top' read as 1.0-1.4 m. Options considered: stage.options (D chosen).

The DJ stands behind a 1.8 x 0.8 m DJ table, 0.95 m high, at the riser's front edge; treads up the left side (toward the backstage); a crowd barrier 1.3 m in front of the riser, 9 m long. The crowd (blue) fills the floor from the barrier to under the crane.

The machinery stays the backdrop: the press (to 5.3 m) stands behind the right half of the riser and the machine line beside it further right, so from the floor the DJ is seen against the press; the goalpost header at 7 m is above the press's crown.
No truss: this version stands every fixture on the floor (the booth line, the pit, the column bases, the press).

Strobes, blinders and hazers are other-supplier lines (the rental house lists none): each is a planning type modelled on a named product (scripts/place/fixtures/fixtures.json, EXT- codes). No CO2 jet, cold spark or confetti — the underground brief (versions file, method).

Each LOOK is one static state for previsualisation (a focus palette), not a show: positions are the rig's, aims and colours the look's. Every lamp but the press's own six mirrors about the nave centre line (x 0), the booth's axis too. Brightness between fixtures follows the datasheets (photometry below); the overall exposure is one chosen number (photometry.sceneScale).

budget.why: A browser cannot run ~90 real three.js spot lights: each is a term in the shader of every lit pixel and, with shadows on, a shadow render and a texture unit each (WebGL gives 16-32; past that every lit material fails to compile). Every fixture draws its beam cone; only these 8 lamps also light the room (the rest of the PARs' light on the columns and the press is baked, wash-glb.mjs), and shadows are OFF by default (the owner found the first version too laggy, 2026-09-27). Measured — see scripts/place/README.md, 'The rig'.
budget.realNote: 2026-09-28 (DJ place): the press's own uplights stand 0.35 m from it, where a real lamp in the renderer blows the face out white; they are baked like the other PARs, and the 4 header spots (6.3 m up, over the DJ and the press) are the real lamps that light the backdrop.

night.note: Darker than the base's readable night (ambient 0.8 -> 0.5, directional 0.35 -> 0.22): darkness is part of the design here (rule 1); the hall must still read in a render. Tuned by eye on the RTX 3080, 2026-09-28.

photometry.method: scripts/place/rig-lib.mjs, 'PHOTOMETRY': candela from the manifest (I = E*d^2 from a measured illuminance, else I = flux / beam solid angle); zoom keeps flux; three.js SpotLight intensity is candela x sceneScale; beam-in-air brightness ~ I*tan(theta/2), scaled to the brightest class, Stevens exponent 1/3, times `air`.
photometry.sceneScaleNote: ONE exposure number for the whole rig, chosen so the room reads in a browser's tone mapping (ACES, exposure 1). The ratios between fixtures are the datasheets'.
photometry.airNote: how much haze is in the air: the brightest class's beam gets this `haze` (0..1, src/objectComponents/spotBeam.js).
photometry.airWhy: Heavy haze (rule 4; 2-6 hazers in every version where the base had 4 smoke machines): every cone's air brightness at 1.5 where the base rig draws 0.9. A drawing choice, not photometry — the ratios between the fixtures stay the datasheets'.

white-cathedral.title: White cathedral
white-cathedral.intent: The roof frame and the columns as a nave of cold white: the column beams stand straight up in mirrored pairs, the booth's line opens a narrow apse fan behind the DJ. Everything else is dark — no PAR, no spot, no strobe.

red-room.title: Red room
red-room.intent: Deep red only, and low: the columns and the press glow from their feet, the booth's beams stand still and dim in red, the DJ a dark shape against the red press. The column beams are out: the roof stays black.

strobe-hit.title: Strobe hit
strobe-hit.intent: The peak: every strobe and blinder at full, white and warm-white, aimed at the crowd from low in the pit and from the booth's height; every beam and PAR out, so the flash lands on black.

one-beam.title: Blackout + one beam
one-beam.intent: Everything out but one: the beam on the floor right behind the DJ, straight up into the roof — the DJ a silhouette cut out of it.

slow-sweep.title: Slow sweep
slow-sweep.intent: A held frame of a slow mirrored sweep: the column beams lean out toward the walls in pairs, the booth's line fans wide; the columns glow a low red underneath. Nothing flashes.

opening.note: the first screen: 18 m out on the dance floor, on the centre line, eye height, looking straight at the booth and the press (owner, 04:13)
